Function: BenchmarkEngine.public static async Task<BenchmarkReport> RunPreparedAsync(string folder, BenchmarkProfile profile, BenchmarkPreparedWorkloadExecutor operation, IProgress<BenchmarkProgress>? progress = null, TimeProvider? timeProvider = null, ILog? log = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
Rationale: RunPreparedAsync: validates folder/profile before any work; warm-up runs and baseline metrics snapshot are excluded from samples (Iterations counts only timed samples); cancellation rethrown, other failures logged then rethrown; samples.Count==0 cannot occur because Validate requires Iterations>=1 and the InsufficientData branch is defensive; elapsed uses injected TimeProvider.GetElapsedTime so no double-rounding; folder is only checked for existence and echoed in the report, never written to. Covered by BenchmarkEngineTimingTests.RunPreparedAsync_SamplesExcludePrepareTime / RunPreparedAsync_MetricsExcludeWarmup. Minor: StartedUtc uses DateTimeOffset.UtcNow while samples use TimeProvider (cosmetic) and Fail/Warn Message text is also set for InsufficientData (unreachable).

Ms: value.ToString("F1", InvariantCulture) so log lines never use the Vietnamese decimal comma (CA1305); NaN/Infinity would print as symbols but inputs are finite elapsed ms or P50 of empty set = 0 (BenchmarkStatistics.Percentile returns 0 for empty). Covered by BenchmarkEngineTimingTests.RunPreparedAsync_LogUsesInvariantDecimals.

Function: BenchmarkImageExecutor.public BenchmarkImageExecutor(BenchmarkProfile profile, string[] files, Func<double, bool>? hasHeadroom = null)
Rationale: Ctor: scratch disk cache dir is Path.GetTempPath()/PhotoReview-Benchmark-Cache/<Guid> so benchmark never reads/writes the real %LocalAppData% preview cache; disableDiskCacheOverride=!profile.DiskCache disables persistence; WindowedPreloadTarget receives the profile windows (PERF-01); FullFolderThresholdBytes is 0 for non-FullFolder profiles so no whole-folder escalation; files[] empty is accepted (Array.ConvertAll of empty). Covered by BenchmarkTrustTests.Executor_HonorsNextAndPreviousWindow / Executor_ZeroWindowWarmsNoNeighbours / Executor_FullFolderControlsWholeFolderWarming.
Lambda `() => isOriginal` captures a local bool copied from profile.LoadingMode at construction; profile is an immutable record so no stale-capture bug.
Lambda `() => profile.TargetWidth()` re-evaluates the Id switch on each call (cheap, pure); returns 0 for original-correctness meaning unbounded; custom ids silently get 1920 (see TargetWidth).
Lambda `f => new CatalogEntry(f)` maps each file path 1:1 into the entry array handed to the scheduler; no path normalisation, WindowedPreloadTarget normalises separately with GetFullPath.
Lambda `() => catalogEntries` returns the same prebuilt array every call, the scheduler snapshot is therefore stable for the whole run (no folder-change simulation, intended for a benchmark).

EvictForColdDecode: evicts the RAM key and the preload-consumed marker, then ClearDisk() which only touches the executor's own scratch _diskCacheDirectory (checked PreviewImageService.ClearDisk uses _diskCacheDirectory), never the user's real cache; called in the untimed prepare step of FirstFrame so the cold decode really comes from source.

Lambda `normalized => _preloadScheduler.RemovePreloadedKeysForPath(normalized)` forwards the normalised key path so a later TryConsumePreloadedKey cannot report a stale preload hit for an evicted path.

Function: BenchmarkImageExecutor.public Task<IDecodedImage> DecodeAsync(string path, CancellationToken token = default)
Rationale: DecodeAsync: ThrowIfCancellationRequested before work (cancellation only between decodes, documented); a preload hit is counted only when the RAM cache already held the key AND the scheduler had marked it preloaded, mirroring MainWindow so Preload/WarmNext hit counts are not inflated. Covered by BenchmarkWorkloadRunnerTests.WarmNextWorkloadRecordsPreloadHitAfterWarming.

Metrics getter returns _metrics.Snapshot(), an immutable record of longs, so the later BenchmarkMetrics.Since subtraction is on a stable copy; thread-safe (ReviewMetrics uses interlocked counters). Covered indirectly by RunPreparedAsync_MetricsExcludeWarmup.

WarmPreloadAround: sets window center then fire-and-forgets PreloadAroundAsync (which swallows its own faults); only the last task is retained, earlier passes are cancelled by the scheduler restart so awaiting only the last in DisposeAsync is sufficient. Covered by BenchmarkTrustTests.Executor_HonorsNextAndPreviousWindow.
IsPreviewCached: test seam, internal, read-only RAM cache probe by current cache key; no side effects.
WhenPreloadSettledAsync: returns _lastPreloadTask or CompletedTask, internal test seam; reading a non-volatile field is fine because tests call it after WarmPreloadAround on the same thread.
DiskCacheDirectory: internal getter of the Guid-named scratch path, used by BenchmarkImageExecutorTeardownTests to assert removal.

DisposeAsync: cancels the scheduler before awaiting the last preload task (bare catch is intentional so a failed preload cannot fail teardown), disposes the scheduler, flushes persist workers (failure logged), then starts the scratch-dir delete on a background task without awaiting; every executor has its own Guid dir so a lingering prune cannot race the next profile. Not idempotent (second call disposes the scheduler again and replaces TeardownBackgroundTask) but harmless because delete is guarded by Directory.Exists. Covered by BenchmarkImageExecutorTeardownTests.DisposeAsync_DoesNotBlockOnPrune_ButStillCleansUpEventually.

DeleteScratchDirectoryAfterPruneAsync: waits up to 2 min for the prune, leaves the dir (logged) if it never settles, deletes only _diskCacheDirectory (own Guid dir under %TEMP%) recursively, all exceptions observed and logged; never touches photo folders. Covered by the teardown test above.

Function: BenchmarkProfileScope.public static IDisposable ApplyLogging(BenchmarkProfile profile, Func<bool> getEnabled, Action<bool> setEnabled, Func<int>? getWriteCount = null)
Rationale: ApplyLogging: null-checks all delegates, records previous state before applying DetailedLogging, restore is skipped when getWriteCount changed (user toggled logging in Settings during the run). Covered by BenchmarkTrustTests.ProfileScope_AppliesAndRestoresLogging / ProfileScope_LoggingChangedDuringRun_IsNotOverwritten.
Restore lambda: compares getWriteCount() with the count captured right after setEnabled, so the benchmark's own write is not mistaken for a foreign one; calls setEnabled(previous) otherwise.
Restore.Dispose: Interlocked.Exchange(ref _restore, null) makes the restore run at most once under double Dispose or concurrent Dispose.

Function: WindowedPreloadTarget.public WindowedPreloadTarget(IPreloadTarget inner, string[] files, BenchmarkProfile profile)
Rationale: WindowedPreloadTarget ctor: indexes files by GetFullPath with OrdinalIgnoreCase (Windows semantics); duplicate paths keep the last index (harmless); a relative path in files is normalised against the current directory consistently with the scheduler only if the scheduler also passes full paths (CatalogEntry(f) uses f as-is, tests use absolute paths); null files would NRE but the only caller passes the same array it built entries from.
SetCenter: Volatile.Write of an int center read by scheduler worker threads in OutsideWindow via Volatile.Read; pairing is correct.

OutsideWindow: FullFolder or unknown path returns false (not restricted), delta=index-center cannot overflow for array-sized ints, window test `delta > _next || -delta > _previous` matches the profile Next/Previous semantics. Covered by BenchmarkTrustTests.Executor_HonorsNextAndPreviousWindow and Executor_ZeroWindowWarmsNoNeighbours.
TryGetCachedPreview(string): reports out-of-window as already cached so the scheduler skips it, otherwise delegates; semantics documented in the class summary.
TryGetCachedPreview(ImageCacheKey): same window check on key.Path, otherwise delegates to the real service; consistent with the string overload.

Function: WindowedPreloadTarget.public Task PreloadAsync(string path, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
Rationale: PreloadAsync: pure forwarder to the inner PreviewImageService, the window is enforced earlier by the cached-preview probes.
GetCurrentCacheKey(string): pure forwarder (the key includes size/mtime so benchmark and production share key identity).
GetCurrentCacheKey(CatalogEntry): pure forwarder to the inner service.
CacheCount: forwarder of the live RAM-cache count, no caching.
CacheBytes: forwarder of the live RAM-cache byte total, used by the scheduler memory/capacity checks.
ActiveViewerDecodes: forwarder so the scheduler yields to viewer decodes exactly as in production.
CachedPreviewBytes: forwarder, returns null when not cached; no window filtering needed because callers already passed the cached probe.
HasDiskCachedPreview: forwarder to the inner service; with DiskCache=false profiles the service answers false so the scheduler never expects disk hits.

Function: BenchmarkMetrics.public static ReviewMetricsSnapshot Since(ReviewMetricsSnapshot current, ReviewMetricsSnapshot baseline)
Rationale: Since subtracts every cumulative counter and handles DecoderFallbacks/PresentHistogram, but TopSourceOpens is only reduced by the baseline's top-10 list (documented): a path opened during warm-up yet outside the baseline top 10 is reported with its full count, so measured-iteration source opens are over-reported while SourceOpenCount (exact total) stays right. See finding BM-01. Also any future ReviewMetricsSnapshot init property not copied here is silently dropped. No test targets BenchmarkMetrics.Since directly except RunPreparedAsync_MetricsExcludeWarmup (totals only).

Since lambda `e => e.Path` (ToDictionary key of baseline.TopSourceOpens, OrdinalIgnoreCase): ReviewMetrics._sourceOpens is a case-insensitive ConcurrentDictionary so keys are unique and ToDictionary cannot throw on duplicates.
Since lambda `e => e.Count` (baseline count value selector): plain long, no overflow concern.
Since lambda `b => b.Label` (baseline histogram key, Ordinal): histogram buckets have unique fixed labels so ToDictionary is safe.
Since lambda `b => b.Count` (baseline histogram value): plain long selector.

Since lambda `e => new SourceOpenEntry(e.Path, e.Count - baselineOpens.GetValueOrDefault(e.Path))`: subtracts only when the baseline listed the path (the BM-01 limitation); result can be <=0 and is filtered by the next Where.
Since lambda `e => e.Count > 0` drops paths with nothing left after subtraction, so negative deltas never reach the report.
Since lambda `e => e.Count` (OrderByDescending): descending by remaining count, deterministic when combined with ThenBy.
Since lambda `e => e.Path` (ThenBy, OrdinalIgnoreCase): stable tie-break so report JSON is deterministic.

Since lambda `b => new PresentLatencyBucket(b.Label, b.Count - baselineBuckets.GetValueOrDefault(b.Label))`: bucket delta, a bucket absent in the baseline subtracts 0 (correct), never negative for cumulative histograms.

Function: BenchmarkProfileExtensions.public static int TargetWidth(this BenchmarkProfile profile)
Rationale: TargetWidth: pure Id switch (960/1600/2400/3200, 0 for original-correctness, 1920 default); a profile with a custom Id silently decodes at 1920 and nothing validates the id list against the registry, acceptable because profiles come from BenchmarkProfiles.All. Covered indirectly by BenchmarkProfileTests.ExpandedBenchmarkProfileRegistry.

Validate: rejects null/blank Id, undefined LoadingMode, Workers<1, negative windows, Iterations<1 with typed BenchmarkProfileException; WarmupCount<0 is not rejected but a negative count just skips the warm-up loop (no failure). Covered by BenchmarkProfileTests (registry/originals) and engine tests that call RunPreparedAsync with valid profiles; no test found for each invalid-settings branch.

Field-initializer lambda `() => Samples.OrderBy(x => x).ToArray()` for the Lazy<double[]> cache: sorts once on first percentile call; Lazy default mode is ExecutionAndPublication so concurrent first reads are safe.

Initializer lambda `x => x` (OrderBy identity key): OrderBy on double sorts NaN first, but samples are finite elapsed ms so ordering is total in practice (Ranking_NaNSamplesDoNotWin covers the corrupt case at rank level).

Private copy constructor: copies every positional property and rebinds a fresh Lazy so `phase with { Samples = ... }` recomputes percentiles from the new samples (the synthesized copy would reuse the original Lazy). Covered by BenchmarkStatisticsEdgeTests.PhaseResult_WithCopyRecomputesStatistics and PhaseResult_WithCopyBeforeForcing. Any future positional member must be added here by hand, a latent maintenance trap not a present bug.
Copy-constructor lambda `() => Samples.OrderBy(...)`: closes over `this` of the copy (not the original) which is exactly the intent; verified by PhaseResult_WithCopyRecomputesStatistics.
Copy-constructor lambda `x => x` identity sort key, same as the field initializer.
Count: Samples.Count, so InsufficientData phases report 0; no division use.

P50: Percentile on the pre-sorted array with .50; empty set returns 0 (BenchmarkStatistics.Percentile) not NaN so JSON stays finite. Covered by BenchmarkStatisticsEdgeTests.PhaseResult_NoSamples / ReportJson_EmptyPhaseIsFinite.
P95: linear-interpolated percentile (not nearest-rank like PerfStats) of sorted samples; one sample returns that sample. Covered by PhaseResult_OneSample and Percentile_SmallSamples.
P99: same interpolation, 0 for empty; with <100 samples interpolates toward max, acceptable for a benchmark. Covered by Percentile_MatchesOracle.
Max: guards Samples.Count==0 returning 0 before indexing _sorted.Value[^1] so no IndexOutOfRange on empty. Covered by PhaseResult_NoSamples.

EffectiveImagesPerSample: Math.Max(1, ...) so P95PerImage never divides by zero; falls back to the profile registry with int.MaxValue file count when the runner did not stamp it (then Workers-based count, possibly more than files actually decoded for tiny folders; runner always stamps so only hand-built phases are affected). Covered by EffectiveImagesPerSample_IsAtLeastOne and Ranking_DerivesImagesPerSampleFromProfile.
P95PerImage: P95 / EffectiveImagesPerSample (>=1) so no divide-by-zero or NaN for finite P95; serialized to the report JSON as a finite number. Covered by Ranking_UsesPerImageUnit.
P50PerImage: P50 / EffectiveImagesPerSample (>=1), same guarantees as P95PerImage.

BenchmarkReport.ToJson: System.Text.Json default writes doubles culture-invariantly (CA1305 satisfied); would throw on NaN/Infinity but every double is a finite percentile or 0 and ReviewMetricsSnapshot has only long counters. Covered by BenchmarkStatisticsEdgeTests.ReportJson_EmptyPhaseIsFinite.
SupportedFileCount: Files.Count, trivial and null-safe because Files is a required positional member.
UnsupportedFileCount: Values.Sum() of ints can in theory overflow int (checked context absent) only past 2 billion files; not realistic.

BenchmarkBatchSummary.ToJson: same default invariant serializer; nested reports/phases serialise their computed percentile properties, all finite. No dedicated test found beyond report-level JSON tests.

Function: BenchmarkRanking.public static IReadOnlyList<BenchmarkPhaseResult> Rank(IEnumerable<BenchmarkPhaseResult> phases, BenchmarkWorkload workload)
Rationale: Rank: filters by workload, excludes Fail and InsufficientData, drops non-finite P95PerImage/P50PerImage (LINQ OrderBy puts NaN first), orders by P95 then P50 per image; stable for ties. Covered by BenchmarkStatisticsEdgeTests.Ranking_NaNSamplesDoNotWin / Ranking_TiesAreStable / Ranking_P95TieBrokenByP50 / Ranking_FiltersByWorkloadAndStatus.
Rank Where lambda: workload equality plus status and finiteness conjunction, order of evaluation harmless because all properties are pure.
Rank OrderBy lambda `x => x.P95PerImage`: ascending like-for-like latency, primary key.
Rank ThenBy lambda `x => x.P50PerImage`: secondary key, verified by Ranking_P95TieBrokenByP50.

IsNotImplemented: `profile.Workload == Correctness && profile.Id is "explorer-reindex" or "cache-recovery"` parses as Id is ("a" or "b") (pattern combinator binds tighter than &&), so only those two Correctness profiles refuse to run; id compared ordinal-case-sensitive while Find is case-insensitive (profiles come from the registry so fine). Covered by BenchmarkProfileTests.Runnable_ExcludesUnimplementedAndCorrectnessOnlyProfiles.

Runnable lambda `p => !p.CorrectnessOnly && !IsNotImplemented(p)`: excludes original-correctness and the two stand-ins from --benchmark-all; static init order is safe because All is declared before Runnable.
Find: case-insensitive id lookup returning null when absent; null id would hit string.Equals(…, null) = false (no throw), blank returns null. Covered by BenchmarkProfileTests.
Find lambda `p => string.Equals(p.Id, id, OrdinalIgnoreCase)`: culture-independent comparison (CA1310 satisfied).

Function: BenchmarkProfiles.private static BenchmarkProfile P(string id, string name, string desc, LoadingMode mode, int workers, int next, int previous, bool full, BenchmarkWorkload workload, long reserve = Reserve, bool detailed = false)
Rationale: P helper: builds a profile with DiskCache=false, WarmupCount default 1 and Iterations default 30; reserve default PerformanceOptions.MemoryReserveBytes; all 30 registry rows pass Validate (Workers>=1, windows>=0), checked by reading the table (low-memory reserve 4 GiB literal uses long math).

UseRealBin: true only when PHOTOREVIEW_BENCH_REAL_RECYCLE_BIN is exactly "1" (Ordinal), so a stray value never enables the real Recycle Bin; evaluated on every call, so changing the env mid-run flips behaviour (documented as opt-in). Covered by BenchmarkRecycleBinTests.Create_Default_DeletesTempCopyWithoutRealBin (default branch only; no test for the opt-in branch found).

Create: null-checks the factory and only invokes realBin() when opted in, so the production WindowsRecycleBin is never constructed by default; default returns TempCopyDeleter. Covered by Create_Default_DeletesTempCopyWithoutRealBin.

TempCopyDeleter.SendToRecycleBin: File.Delete(path) is a permanent delete, safe only because the sole caller (PrepareFileActionAsync) passes its own Guid-named temp copy under %TEMP%; the class is private so nothing else can reach it; File.Delete of a missing file does not throw, so a race where the file is already gone is benign.

Function: BenchmarkRecycleBin.TempCopyDeleter.public bool TryRestore(string originalPath, long expectedSize, DateTime expectedLastWriteUtc)
Rationale: TempCopyDeleter.TryRestore: returns false (nothing to restore for a permanently deleted temp copy); no benchmark workload calls restore.

Function: BenchmarkWorkloadRunner.public static Task<BenchmarkReport> RunProfileAsync(string folder, BenchmarkProfile profile, BenchmarkImageExecutor executor, string[] files, Random random, IRecycleBin recycleBin, IProgress<BenchmarkProgress>? progress = null, CancellationToken ct = default)
Rationale: Public RunProfileAsync: wires PrepareIterationAsync into the shared engine with the folder file count for ImagesPerSample stamping; files.Length is read eagerly (null files NRE, empty files are not rejected here, see BW-01). Covered by BenchmarkTrustTests.RunProfileAsync_StampsImagesPerSample and BenchmarkEngineTimingTests.RunProfileAsync_SamplesExcludeSetupTime.

Lambda `(workload, iteration, token) => PrepareIterationAsync(executor, files, profile, ...)`: closes over the shared Random, so SelectIndex/SelectParallelIndices consume it in the untimed prepare step on a single sequential loop (engine awaits each iteration), no concurrent Random use.

Function: BenchmarkWorkloadRunner.internal static Task<BenchmarkReport> RunProfileAsync(string folder, BenchmarkProfile profile, Func<BenchmarkWorkload, int, CancellationToken, Task<Func<Task<(bool Correct, ReviewMetricsSnapshot? Metrics)>>>> prepare, IProgress<BenchmarkProgress>? progress, TimeProvider? timeProvider, CancellationToken ct, int fileCount = int.MaxValue)
Rationale: Internal RunProfileAsync test seam: adapts the 3-arg prepare to the 4-arg engine delegate and passes the injected TimeProvider; fileCount defaults to int.MaxValue so ImagesPerSample is Workers-based when tests do not care. Covered by RunProfileAsync_SamplesExcludeSetupTime.
Lambda `(_, workload, iteration, token) => prepare(workload, iteration, token)` discards the profile parameter because the closure already carries the profile; no behavioural risk.

Function: BenchmarkWorkloadRunner.private static async Task<BenchmarkReport> StampImagesPerSample(Task<BenchmarkReport> run, BenchmarkProfile profile, int fileCount)
Rationale: StampImagesPerSample: awaits the run then rebuilds Phases with ImagesPerSample stamped per phase workload; if the run throws the exception propagates untouched. Covered by BenchmarkTrustTests.RunProfileAsync_StampsImagesPerSample.
Lambda `p => p with { ImagesPerSample = ... }` uses the explicit copy constructor so percentile caches are rebuilt (see F01251).

Function: BenchmarkWorkloadRunner.public static int ImagesPerSample(BenchmarkProfile profile, BenchmarkWorkload workload, int fileCount)
Rationale: ImagesPerSample: 1 for FirstFrame/Preload/WarmNext/FileAction, else min(Workers,fileCount) with both clamped to >=1, so the divisor in P95PerImage is never 0 even for empty folders. Covered by BenchmarkStatisticsEdgeTests.ImagesPerSample_Table / ImagesPerSample_AgreesWithSelectedIndices.

Function: BenchmarkWorkloadRunner.public static async Task<Func<Task<(bool Correct, ReviewMetricsSnapshot? Metrics)>>> PrepareIterationAsync( BenchmarkImageExecutor executor, string[] files, BenchmarkProfile profile, BenchmarkWorkload workload, int iteration, Random random, IRecycleBin recycleBin, CancellationToken ct)
Rationale: PrepareIterationAsync: correct dispatch (not-implemented guard first, FileAction, FirstFrame with untimed cold eviction, Preload/WarmNext single navigation step, otherwise bounded Parallel.ForEachAsync), but with files.Length==0 behaviour is inconsistent: FirstFrame/Preload/WarmNext throw DivideByZero/IndexOutOfRange from SelectIndex while the parallel path builds zero-length selected[] and `results.All` of an empty array returns true, i.e. a Pass with nothing decoded. Both front ends guard empty folders today (BenchmarkWindow files.Length==0, Cli Program.cs), so this is a public-API robustness gap only. See BW-01. Covered partly by BenchmarkWorkloadRunnerTests; no empty-folder test found.

FirstFrame measure lambda: decodes the path chosen in prepare and requires PixelWidth>0 and PixelHeight>0, returns executor.Metrics; the cold eviction (RAM+scratch disk) happened untimed in prepare so the sample is a true first decode. ct is captured, cancellation checked only before decode (documented).

Preload/WarmNext measure lambda: calls executor.WarmPreloadAround(center) INSIDE the timed measure step after the decode, so the synchronous portion of PreloadAroundAsync (window snapshot, CTS replace, task start) is added to every sample, whereas production does it after the frame is presented. Small but systematic and only for these two workloads, skewing their P50/P95 against Sequential/FirstFrame. See BW-03 (NEEDS-EVIDENCE: magnitude not measured). No test isolates it.
Lambda `i => files[i]` (Array.ConvertAll over SelectParallelIndices result): indices come from SelectIndex bounded by fileCount, so in range whenever files is non-empty.

Parallel measure lambda: runs at most `count`=min(Workers,files.Length) decodes concurrently with the run CancellationToken; per-index results array has one writer per slot so no race; returns executor.Metrics after all complete. Sample wall time therefore covers Workers parallel decodes, which is why ImagesPerSample divides by Workers. Covered by BenchmarkStatisticsEdgeTests.ImagesPerSample_AgreesWithSelectedIndices.

ForEachAsync body `(idx, ct2) => decode selected[idx]`: writes results[idx] only after the decode returns; a decode exception faults the whole ForEachAsync and propagates to the engine (logged and rethrown), no partial Pass.
Lambda `r => r` (results.All): all images must decode with positive size to be Correct; vacuously true only for an empty selection (BW-01).

Function: BenchmarkWorkloadRunner.private static async Task<Func<Task<(bool Correct, ReviewMetricsSnapshot? Metrics)>>> PrepareFileActionAsync( BenchmarkImageExecutor executor, string[] files, BenchmarkProfile profile, int iteration, IRecycleBin recycleBin, CancellationToken ct)
Rationale: PrepareFileActionAsync: untimed setup copies the chosen photo into a Guid-named .bin under %TEMP% (File.ReadAllBytesAsync then WriteAllBytesAsync, source opened read-only, never modified); the setup catch calls Cleanup() and rethrows; measure step mutates only temp/moved/copied paths and Cleanup runs in finally; no path ever points into the photo folder or touches the real Recycle Bin unless the opt-in env var is set. Reading the whole source file into memory is acceptable for a benchmark (RAW 100 MB). Covered by BenchmarkWorkloadRunnerTests.FileActionProfilePerformsItsOwnOperation and PrepareIterationAsync_FileAction_ActionRunsOnlyInMeasureStep.

Cleanup local function: deletes exactly temp, temp+".moved", temp+".copy" (all own Guid names), each guarded by File.Exists and a catch limited to IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException so a locked file (decoder still holding it) is left for the OS temp cleaner instead of failing the run; a leftover file is the only consequence.

File-action measure lambda: starts the real decode then mutates temp (move+delete / recycleBin.SendToRecycleBin / copy), observes the decode task in every path (no unobserved fault), swallows only IO/UnauthorizedAccess/NotSupported/FileFormat decode failures while rethrowing cancellation, and checks the filesystem contract (source gone for move/delete, present for copy). Suspect only: the scratch file is always named *.bin, so FormatRoutingDecoder routes by extension to the standard decoder; for a RAW source (.cr2/.nef) that decoder throws NotSupported/FileFormat, which is swallowed, so Correct depends only on File.Exists and the profile can Pass without ever exercising a decode. Not proven because BenchmarkImageExecutor uses the default decoder in tests. See BW-04. Covered by BenchmarkWorkloadRunnerTests.FileActionProfilePerformsItsOwnOperation, InterleavedActionProfileCyclesThroughAllThreeOperations.

CreateSeededRandom: new Random(StableHash(profileId)) so each profile replays the same file sequence across processes (string.GetHashCode is randomised per process). Covered by BenchmarkSelectionGoldenTests.CreateSeededRandom_YieldsGoldenSequence.

StableHash: unchecked 31-multiplier hash over UTF-16 chars, overflow wraps by design, empty string yields 17, deterministic across processes; collisions only mean two profiles share a sequence, harmless. Golden-tested.

Function: BenchmarkWorkloadRunner.internal static int[] SelectParallelIndices(int fileCount, BenchmarkProfile profile, BenchmarkWorkload workload, int iteration, Random random)
Rationale: SelectParallelIndices: count=min(max(1,Workers),fileCount) and one SelectIndex per slot with iteration+offset, consuming the shared Random in prepare (untimed), correct for fileCount>=1; with fileCount==0 it returns an empty array so the caller reports a vacuous Pass instead of failing (BW-01). Covered by BenchmarkSelectionGoldenTests.RandomWorkload_SelectsGoldenFileIndices and BenchmarkStatisticsEdgeTests.ImagesPerSample_AgreesWithSelectedIndices.

Lambda `o => SelectIndex(fileCount, workload, iteration + o, random)`: Enumerable.Select over Range is lazy but materialised by ToArray in the same statement, so Random is consumed in deterministic order (offset 0..count-1), which the golden test relies on.

Function: BenchmarkWorkloadRunner.private static string SelectFile(string[] files, BenchmarkWorkload workload, int iteration, Random random)
Rationale: SelectFile: files[SelectIndex(...)] throws IndexOutOfRange/DivideByZero for an empty array (Random.Next(0) returns 0 then files[0] fails); only FirstFrame uses it and callers pre-check emptiness, so latent (BW-01). Covered indirectly by FirstFrame tests; none for empty.

Function: BenchmarkWorkloadRunner.private static int SelectIndex(int fileCount, BenchmarkWorkload workload, int iteration, Random random)
Rationale: SelectIndex: Random uses random.Next(fileCount); Preload uses iteration*2 % fileCount (iteration*2 cannot overflow for realistic Iterations); `iteration / 2 % fileCount` evaluates as (iteration/2)%fileCount, intended. Suspect: WarmNext alternates iteration 0->0, 1->n-1, 2->1, 3->n-2 so consecutive navigation centres jump across the whole folder instead of stepping forward, and each WarmPreloadAround(center) cancels the previous pass, so a preload hit for the 'next' image is only possible in tiny folders; profile names (WarmNext, fast-balanced, rapid-key-press) suggest sequential next-image navigation. Not proven: intent may be forward+backward coverage and hit rate was not measured. See BW-02. Golden tests cover Random only; WarmNext sequence is not asserted anywhere (BenchmarkStatisticsEdgeTests only checks the images-per-sample table).

Function: SlowLinkFileSystem.public SlowLinkFileSystem(IFileSystem inner, TimeSpan metadataLatency, SharedBandwidthLimiter? bandwidth)
Rationale: SlowLinkFileSystem ctor: null inner rejected, negative latency rejected via ThrowIfLessThan(TimeSpan.Zero), bandwidth may be null (latency-only mode). Covered by SlowLinkFileSystemTests.

DelayMetadata: Thread.Sleep only when latency>0; blocking sleep is intentional because the wrapped IFileSystem API is synchronous; harness-only (wired by the CLI --perf-session --slow-link-*), never a production default.
FileExists: delay then delegate; order matters little for a latency model.
DirectoryExists: delay then delegate.
GetFileStat: delay then delegate, returns null for a missing file as the inner does.

Function: SlowLinkFileSystem.public void Move(string source, string destination)
Rationale: Move: untouched forwarder; no benchmark scenario mutates across the simulated link; forwarding avoids any chance of the decorator swallowing a data-affecting call. Covered by FileSystemWrapperForwardingTests.

Function: SlowLinkFileSystem.public void Copy(string source, string destination)
Rationale: Copy: untouched forwarder, same reasoning as Move.

Function: SlowLinkFileSystem.public bool TryCopyNew(string source, string destination)
Rationale: TryCopyNew(source,destination): explicitly forwarded instead of the interface default (exists-check + Copy, non-atomic) so the create-new semantics of PhysicalFileSystem survive behind this decorator. Covered by FileSystemWrapperForwardingTests.EveryFileSystemDecorator_ForwardsTheCreateNewPrimitivesToTheInnerFileSystem.
Delete: untouched forwarder to the inner permanent delete; not delayed, not intercepted.

Function: SlowLinkFileSystem.public Stream OpenReadShared(string path, int bufferSize = 65536)
Rationale: OpenReadShared: wraps the inner stream in ThrottledReadStream only when a limiter is configured; the wrapper owns/disposes the inner stream. Documented in Q-R29-C as unreachable from the real decode path (SlowLinkSourceReader is the effective seam).

Function: SlowLinkFileSystem.public Stream OpenAppend(string path, bool durable)
Rationale: OpenAppend: untouched forwarder (journal/session writes are not simulated as slow).

Function: SlowLinkFileSystem.public void WriteAllTextAtomic(string path, string text, bool durable = true)
Rationale: WriteAllTextAtomic: untouched forwarder preserving the atomic temp-and-rename behaviour of the inner.
ReadAllText: untouched forwarder, not metered or delayed (settings/session small files).

Function: SlowLinkFileSystem.public IEnumerable<string> EnumerateFiles(string directory, string pattern = "*")
Rationale: EnumerateFiles: forwarder without delay; the per-entry delays are modelled in the WithStat overloads, which is what folder open uses.

Function: SlowLinkFileSystem.public IEnumerable<(string Path, FileStat? Stat)> EnumerateFilesWithStat( string directory, Func<string, bool> include, Action<SkippedEntry> onSkipped)
Rationale: EnumerateFilesWithStat: iterator that delays once per entry after the inner yields it; delay is only charged for entries passing include (the inner filters), so excluded files cost no simulated latency (slightly optimistic vs a real NAS, harmless for the harness). Argument null checks are deferred to the inner iterator. Covered by SlowLinkFileSystemTests.EnumerateReadableFilesWithStat_AppliesMetadataLatencyPerEntry (readable variant).

Function: SlowLinkFileSystem.public bool TryProbeReadable(string path, out string? failure)
Rationale: TryProbeReadable: delay then delegate with the out failure flowing through unchanged.

Function: SlowLinkFileSystem.public IEnumerable<(string Path, FileStat? Stat)> EnumerateReadableFilesWithStat( string directory, Func<string, bool> include, Action<SkippedEntry> onSkipped)
Rationale: EnumerateReadableFilesWithStat: delegates to the inner readable enumerator (so the probe uses the inner implementation, not this class's delayed TryProbeReadable) and delays per yielded entry; onSkipped forwarded unchanged. Covered by SlowLinkFileSystemTests.EnumerateReadableFilesWithStat_AppliesMetadataLatencyPerEntry.
EnumerateDirectories: undelayed forwarder, lazily enumerated by the inner.
CreateDirectory: undelayed forwarder.
ResolveRealPath: delay then delegate; keeps SEC-01 reparse-point resolution of the inner (decorator does not fall back to the Path.GetFullPath default).

Consume: ignores bytes<=0, chunks requests larger than one second's budget (bucket is capped at bytesPerSecond) so it cannot spin forever, (int) cast is safe because chunk<=remaining<=int.MaxValue. No dedicated unit test found beyond SlowLinkFileSystemTests/PreloadSlowLinkViewerPriorityTests (Imaging) exercising it indirectly.

ConsumeChunk: refill and take under a lock, sleep outside the lock so concurrent readers share the budget; wait=missing/bytesPerSecond seconds clamped to >=1 ms, `missing` is bounded by bytes<=bps so the wait is <=1 s; loop terminates because refill accumulates. Wall-clock based, see Refill.

Refill: uses DateTime.UtcNow ticks (not monotonic, a clock step backwards makes elapsed<=0 and only re-bases _lastTicks, a step forward just fills the bucket up to its 1-second cap); _availableBytes starts at 0 and _lastTicks at construction, so the first read after a long idle gets at most one second of burst. Acceptable for a measurement harness; Stopwatch would be stricter.
ThrottledReadStream.CanRead: forwards inner.CanRead.
CanSeek: forwards inner.CanSeek, so callers may Seek on the wrapped stream; bytes consumed by seeks are not metered (reads only).
CanWrite: constant false, consistent with Write throwing NotSupportedException.
Length: forwards inner.Length; used by pre-read code (new byte[fileStream.Length]), unmetered which is correct because no bytes are transferred.
Position getter: forwards inner.Position.
Position setter: forwards to inner.Position (seek is free, only reads cost tokens).

Function: ThrottledReadStream.public override int Read(byte[] buffer, int offset, int count)
Rationale: Read(byte[],int,int): reads first then consumes `read` tokens when read>0, so the throttle delays after the data is obtained (average rate is right, first read is not delayed); other paths (ReadByte, CopyTo, ReadAsync) funnel into this override via the Stream base, so no unmetered route exists.
Read(Span<byte>): same read-then-consume model; kept as a separate override because Stream.Read(Span) default would rent a buffer and call Read(byte[]) anyway, behaviour identical.

Function: ThrottledReadStream.public override long Seek(long offset, SeekOrigin origin)
Rationale: Seek: forwards to inner.Seek, no metering.
SetLength: forwards to the inner stream, which for a read-only file stream throws NotSupportedException as expected; never called on read paths.

Function: ThrottledReadStream.public override void Write(byte[] buffer, int offset, int count)
Rationale: Write: throws NotSupportedException, correct for a read-only decorator (CanWrite is false).
Flush: forwards inner.Flush(); harmless on a read-only stream.
Dispose(bool): disposes the inner stream only when disposing==true and always calls base.Dispose; the inner is owned by this wrapper so there is no leak or double-dispose (inner Dispose idempotent).
SlowLinkSourceReader ctor: rejects null inner, accepts null limiter (pass-through mode); no other state.

Function: SlowLinkSourceReader.public Stream OpenSource(string path, SourceReadPriority priority, int bufferSize = 1024 * 1024)
Rationale: OpenSource: opens the inner stream then wraps with the shared limiter when configured; priority is passed through but ignored by design (documented measurement decorator); bufferSize default 1 MiB matches ISourceReader. No direct test found (covered through Imaging PreloadSlowLinkViewerPriorityTests).

Function: NaNAsNullDoubleConverter.public override double Read(ref Utf8JsonReader reader, Type typeToConvert, JsonSerializerOptions options)
Rationale: NaNAsNullDoubleConverter.Read: maps JSON null to NaN, otherwise reader.GetDouble() (throws InvalidOperationException on a string token, acceptable because only this tool's own summary.json is read); round-trips with Write. Covered by PerfAnalyzeReportTests (JSON written through it) but no direct Read test found.

Function: NaNAsNullDoubleConverter.public override void Write(Utf8JsonWriter writer, double value, JsonSerializerOptions options)
Rationale: NaNAsNullDoubleConverter.Write: finite values written as numbers, NaN and +/-Infinity as null so System.Text.Json never throws on empty-group percentiles; null-checks writer. Applies to double? too (NullableConverter wraps it). Covered by PerfAnalyzeTests.PerfAnalyzeWithOnlyIncompleteNavsStillWritesJson.

IsBurstScenario: strips the @folderAlias suffix, requires S3/S4 prefix (case-insensitive) and that the third char is not a digit so S30/pics3 do not count; null key gives an empty span and false. Covered by PerfAnalyzeTests.BurstScenarioMatchesTheScenarioPartOnly.

Function: PerfAnalyze.public static Task<AnalysisResult> RunAsync(string runDir, string? rulesPath)
Rationale: RunAsync: returns Task but runs all CSV parsing and the summary writes synchronously on the caller thread and throws (DirectoryNotFound/InvalidOperation/InvalidData) synchronously instead of returning a faulted Task; a caller that composes the task without awaiting immediately would miss the throw, and a UI-thread caller would block. Output goes only to runDir/summary.md and summary.json (overwritten without prompt), never to a photo folder; warmup directories are excluded; per-file failures are wrapped in InvalidDataException naming the file. See PA-04. Covered by PerfAnalyzeTests.PerfAnalyzeOnTheSampleDirectoryWritesSummaryMdAndJson, PerfAnalyzeThrowsWhenNoCsvFilesArePresent, PerfAnalyzeKeepsWorkerTreatmentsSeparateAndOnlyComparesSameCondition.

RunAsync Where lambda `p => !GetRelativePath(runDir,p).Split(sep).Any(...)`: excludes any csv under a path segment named warmup (case-insensitive) relative to runDir, so a runDir that itself lives under a folder called warmup is not wrongly empty; splitting on DirectorySeparatorChar only (EnumerateFiles returns the platform separator on Windows).
Inner lambda `part => string.Equals(part,"warmup",OrdinalIgnoreCase)`: culture-independent segment match, whole-segment so "warmup2" is kept.
OrderBy lambda `p => p` with StringComparer.Ordinal: deterministic file order independent of locale, so aggregated groups are reproducible.

GroupBy lambda `n => IsNullOrEmpty(n.Mode) ? "unknown" : n.Mode` with Ordinal comparer: majority vote of ShowStart.mode per file; ties are resolved by OrderByDescending stability on first-seen group (deterministic for a given file).
OrderByDescending lambda `g => g.Count()` for the mode majority vote; ties keep first group, deterministic.
Select lambda `key => GroupSummary.Build(key, groupNavs[key])`: key always exists because it is enumerated from groupNavs.Keys; no KeyNotFound.

Lambda `m => m.GcTimePercent` feeding AverageOrNull: unweighted mean of per-run values, nulls ignored; a run with NaN/negative gc percent from a hand-edited process.json would pull the mean but is not validated (see RunFileMeta.Load).
Lambda `m => m.FrameTimeP95Ms`: same unweighted mean of per-run P95s (a mean of P95s is not a pooled P95; acceptable proxy for the R-UI frame threshold, documented as per-run metadata).
OrderBy lambda `r => r.Summary.Key.Scenario` (Ordinal): primary sort of result groups, deterministic.
ThenBy lambda `...Key.Mode` (Ordinal): secondary sort key.
ThenBy lambda `...Key.Cond` (Ordinal): tertiary sort key.

ThenBy lambda `PreloadWorkers ?? -1`: numeric worker order with unknown first, avoiding the text-sort 10-before-2 bug. Covered by PerfAnalyzeReportTests.GroupsAreOrderedByWorkerCountNumericallyNotAsText.

Function: PerfAnalyze.private static List<RuleResult> EvaluateAllRules(RulesConfig rules, GroupSummary s, List<GroupSummary> allGroups)
Rationale: EvaluateAllRules: filters Incomplete navs once, passes plain aggregates to the nine PerfRules evaluators; empty sets give NaN/null (not division by zero): nonRamHitSharePct guards complete.Count>0, ramHitFinalP95 NaN when no RamHit; R-CONT picks min/max PreloadWorkers siblings with identical scenario/mode/cond, so single-sibling groups compare against themselves and EvaluateRCont returns N/A via lowWorkers==highWorkers. Every group in a family receives the same R-CONT verdict (including a group with unknown workers) which is documented behaviour. Covered by PerfAnalyzeTests.PerfAnalyzeKeepsWorkerTreatmentsSeparateAndOnlyComparesSameCondition and the R* rule tests.
Lambda `n => !n.Incomplete`: only navigations with a matched final Presented feed rules, consistent with GroupSummary percentiles.
Lambda sourceMissNavs Where `Kind.Contains("SourceMiss", Ordinal)`: matches both SourceMiss and Thumbnail+SourceMiss, culture-independent.
Lambda decodeNavs Where (SourceMiss or InflightJoin): deliberately includes joined decodes for R-DEC; consistent with AverageDecodeMs.
Lambda ramHitNavs Where `Kind.Contains("RamHit")`: includes Thumbnail+RamHit.
Lambda diskCacheHitNavs Where `Kind.Contains("DiskCacheHit")`: includes the Thumbnail+ prefixed kind.
Lambda `n => n.FinalVisualMs is not null` for RamHit P95: only navs with a final time contribute, avoiding a null deref in the next Select.
Lambda `n => n.FinalVisualMs!.Value`: safe because the preceding Where excludes nulls.
Lambda `v => v` OrderBy: ascending order required by PerfStats.NearestRank; doubles are finite (ParseDouble rejects NaN/Inf).
Lambda `n => n.TInputMs is not null` selecting navs with a matched KeyInput.
Lambda `n => n.TInputMs!.Value`: safe after the null filter.
Lambda `v => v` ascending sort for the t_input P95.

Lambda `d => d.Ms > dispatcherThreshold`: strict greater-than with threshold from rules (default 16 ms); counts only rows after the first ShowStart/Folder(start) because the builder excluded earlier ones.

Lambda `g => g.Key.Scenario == s.Key.Scenario && Mode && Cond && PreloadWorkers.HasValue`: restricts R-CONT to the same scenario, mode and condition so cold/warm cells are never compared as a worker experiment; string == is ordinal (CA1310-safe).
Lambda `g => g.PreloadWorkers` OrderBy: low-worker group; nullables excluded by the Where above.
Lambda `g => g.PreloadWorkers` OrderByDescending: high-worker group, ties resolved by first element.

AverageDecodeMs: mean TDecodeMs over complete SourceMiss/InflightJoin navs, null when none, so R-CONT is N/A rather than comparing zeros; inherits the decode-minus-read adjustment issue PA-01 under PHOTOREVIEW_DIAG_PREREAD (not a defect of this function).
Lambda in AverageDecodeMs Where: same kind filter as decodeNavs plus HasValue guard so `.Value` in the Select is safe.
Lambda `n => n.TDecodeMs!.Value`: safe after the HasValue filter.

Function: PerfAnalyze.private static List<T> Add<TKey, T>(Dictionary<TKey, List<T>> dict, TKey key) where TKey : notnull
Rationale: Add<TKey,T>: get-or-create list helper, returns the stored list so AddRange mutates the dictionary entry; not thread-safe but RunAsync is single-threaded.
AverageOrNull: ignores nulls and returns null on an empty set (no Average-on-empty InvalidOperationException).
Lambda `v => v.HasValue`: null filter for the average.
Lambda `v => v!.Value`: safe after the filter.

PerfRow.ANum: delegates to ParseDouble (invariant culture, finite only), so a row with blank or garbage column a reads as absent rather than 0 or NaN. Covered by BenchmarkStatisticsEdgeTests.PerfRow_NonFiniteNumbersAreNull / PerfRow_FiniteNumbersParse.
PerfRow.BNum: same ParseDouble path, used for queue wait in PreloadItem.
PerfRow.CNum: same ParseDouble path, used for preload decode ms.
PerfRow.DNum: same ParseDouble path; no current consumer, harmless.

PerfRow.NavId: long.TryParse Integer with InvariantCulture, null for blank or malformed nav column (such rows are not attached to a navigation); negative -1 preload nav ids parse and are filtered later by navId>0.

ParseDouble: NumberStyles.Float with InvariantCulture and IsFinite rejection, so 'NaN', 'Infinity' and 1e999 overflow become null and cannot poison sorting or percentiles; empty string guarded. Covered by PerfRow_NonFiniteNumbersAreNull.

QpcToMs: deltaTicks*1000.0/QpcFrequency; QpcFrequency is guaranteed >0 by PerfCsvReader.Read (falls back to Stopwatch.Frequency), so no divide-by-zero; fallback is wrong only if a CSV from another machine lacks the header frequency.

PerfCsvReader.Read: streams File.ReadLines, skips blanks/header/comments, tolerates torn or short lines (<11 fields) and non-numeric leading columns, parses the dropped trailer; writer replaces newlines in fields so the line-based read cannot split a quoted record. Read-only access, no writes. Missing file raises FileNotFoundException which RunAsync wraps. Covered by PerfAnalyzeTests.ParsesDataRowsAndSkipsCommentsAndHeader / ReadsDroppedCountFromTrailerComment.

Function: PerfCsvReader.private static void ParseCommentLine(string line, Dictionary<string, string> diagFlags, ref long qpcFrequency, ref long dropped)
Rationale: ParseCommentLine: splits the comment on spaces, handles qpcFrequency/dropped/diag with invariant TryParse, ignores unknown tokens and a '=' at index 0; a later 'dropped=' line overwrites an earlier one (the trailer is written once) and diag values containing spaces would be truncated (not produced by the writer). Covered by ReadsDroppedCountFromTrailerComment.

SplitCsvLine: state machine for quoted fields with doubled quotes, matches PerfCsvListener.CsvEscape (quotes only at field boundaries); a stray quote mid-field in hand-edited input would flip inQuotes, producing a short row that Read then skips; no exceptions possible. Covered indirectly by ParsesDataRowsAndSkipsCommentsAndHeader.

KeyInputIndex ctor: buckets KeyInput rows per thread and sorts each bucket by QpcTicks with stable OrderBy, so equal timestamps keep file order; an empty input yields an empty dictionary. Covered by PerfAnalyzeReportTests.KeyInputMatchingAgreesWithTheBruteForceDefinition.
Ctor lambda `k => k.Thread`: GroupBy key (int thread id).
Ctor lambda `g => g.Key` ToDictionary key selector; keys unique after GroupBy.
Ctor lambda `g => g.OrderBy(...).ToArray()` ToDictionary value selector: materialised sorted array per thread.
Ctor lambda `k => k.QpcTicks` stable sort key.

Function: KeyInputIndex.public PerfRow? NearestAtOrBefore(int thread, long qpcTicks)
Rationale: NearestAtOrBefore: binary-searches the first row with QpcTicks > qpcTicks, returns null when none at or before, then maps back to the FIRST row among equal best timestamps, matching the old OrderByDescending.First semantics. Covered by KeyInputMatchingAgreesWithTheBruteForceDefinition.
Lambda `r => r.QpcTicks > qpcTicks`: monotone false-then-true over the sorted array, as FirstIndexWhere requires.
Lambda `r => r.QpcTicks >= best`: finds the first element of the equal-timestamp run, also monotone.

Function: KeyInputIndex.private static int FirstIndexWhere(PerfRow[] rows, Func<PerfRow, bool> predicate)
Rationale: FirstIndexWhere: lo/hi binary search with (lo+hi)>>>1 (no overflow), returns rows.Length when the predicate never holds; callers handle that (upper==0 check, and rows[...] index of best always exists).

Build: single pass to find the earliest ShowStart/Folder(start) qpc, a second pass bucketing rows by event; DispatcherLongOp rows before that point are counted and excluded; only nav>0 rows join navigations; (int)(ANum??0) for the preload slot can saturate/undefined only for absurd values (a hand-edited CSV); firstPresented maps onto the Startup timeline via the anchor row. Pure on in-memory rows, no file writes. Covered by PerfAnalyzeTests.MatchesKeyInputToShowStartAndComputesFirstAndFinalVisual, AggregatesPreloadItemsDispatcherAndPausedCounters, ExcludesDispatcherLongOpsBeforeTheFirstShowStartOrFolderStart, BuildsStartupMilestonesAndMapsFirstPresentedOntoTheProcessStartTimeline.
Lambda `p => p.QpcTicks` for MinBy of presentedGlobal: earliest Presented across the file, guarded by presentedGlobal.Count>0 so the null-forgiving operator is safe.

Function: PerfAnalyzeNavBuilder.private static void BuildFolderSummaries(PerfCsvFile file, List<PerfRow> folderRows, List<PerfRow> presentedGlobal, List<FolderGenSummary> output)
Rationale: BuildFolderSummaries: groups Folder rows by gen string, skips non-numeric gens, T1/T3 from the named phase rows, T2 = first Presented at or after the start row's qpc using the file's own frequency; missing phases leave nulls instead of zeros. O(gens x presented) is fine for these sizes. Covered by PerfAnalyzeTests.BuildsFolderT0ToT2FromTheEarliestPresentedAfterFolderStart.
Lambda `r => r.Nav` GroupBy key (raw nav column string), parsed to long right after.
Lambda `r => r.QpcTicks` OrderBy for chronological phase rows.
Lambda `r => r.Text == "catalogReady"`: ordinal string equality (== on strings is ordinal), first match wins.
Lambda `r => r.Text is "explorerApplied" or "explorerFallback" or "explorerIgnored"`: first of the three terminal phases, ordinal pattern match.
Lambda `r => r.Text == "start"` locating T0 of the generation.
Lambda `p => p.QpcTicks >= start.QpcTicks`: Presented at or after T0 (same-tick counts), correct direction.
Lambda `p => p.QpcTicks` OrderBy so FirstOrDefault returns the earliest.

Function: PerfAnalyzeNavBuilder.private static NavRecord BuildNavRecord(PerfCsvFile file, long navId, List<PerfRow> rows, KeyInputIndex keyInputs)
Rationale: BuildNavRecord: reassembles a navigation from its rows (ShowStart mode, KeyInput match within 500 ms, first/final Presented relative to t0, thumbnail source preference, RenderedFrame), safe on ordered[0] because rows is never empty. BUT the final block `if TReadMs and TDecodeMs exist then TDecodeMs = max(0, decode - read)` assumes the Decode event also covers the pre-read reported by SourceRead; on current master PreviewImageService.DecodeFromSource starts perfT0 AFTER the pre-read and emits SourceRead before it, so Decode never contains the read and t_decode is understated by t_read (floored at 0), skewing R-DEC, R-DISK, slowest-decile phase shares and R-CONT under PHOTOREVIEW_DIAG_PREREAD=1. See PA-01 with a test sketch. No test covers the subtraction.
Lambda `r => r.QpcTicks` stable OrderBy of the navigation's rows.
Lambda `r => r.Event == "ShowStart"`: first ShowStart row; absent ShowStart falls back to the first row's qpc as t0, so FinalVisual is still defined.

ClassifyKind: maps Lookup result to RamHit/InflightJoin/DiskCacheHit/SourceMiss with the Thumbnail+ prefix; 'miss' without DiskCacheRead or Decode is classed InflightJoin, unknown lookups 'Unknown'. Note TDecodeMs is evaluated after the PA-01 adjustment, but HasValue is unaffected (Math.Max keeps a value). Covered by PerfAnalyzeTests.ClassifiesEveryNavInTheSampleCsv.

Function: PerfAnalyzeReport.public static void WriteMarkdown(string path, PerfAnalyze.AnalysisResult result)
Rationale: WriteMarkdown: all numbers via FormattableString.Invariant or explicit InvariantCulture (CA1305 satisfied), NaN/null rendered as N/A, '|' and newlines escaped in group keys, kinds, phases and evidence, tables skip empty groups safely (no Average/Max on empty: PercentileOrNaN guards). Writes one file via File.WriteAllText (non-atomic, UTF-8 without BOM) to the caller-supplied path inside runDir. Covered by PerfAnalyzeReportTests.PipeInAGroupNameIsEscapedSoTheTableKeepsItsColumns, DroppedRowsAreSurfacedInMarkdownAndJson, RUiEvidenceShowsNaForAnAbsentRamHitP95.
Lambda `g => g.Summary.DroppedRows > 0`: emits the listener-overflow warning only for groups that lost events. Covered by DroppedRowsAreSurfacedInMarkdownAndJson / NoDroppedRowsMeansNoWarning.
Lambda `kv => kv.Value` OrderByDescending of KindCounts: ties keep dictionary insertion order (deterministic per run).
Lambda `kv => kv.Value` OrderByDescending of SlowestPhaseShare for the phase-share table.
Lambda `p => p.QueueWaitMs` selects queue waits; values are finite (ParseDouble) or 0.
Lambda `v => v` sorts queue waits ascending for NearestRank.
Lambda `p => p.Kind == "decoded"` restricts decode percentiles to decoded items (ordinal equals).
Lambda `p => p.Ms` selects preload decode ms.
Lambda `v => v` ascending sort for decode percentiles.
Lambda `d => d.Name` GroupBy of dispatcher ops by name for the top-5 table; names are escaped when printed.
Lambda `gr => (Name, Count, Total)` Select: tuple of count and summed ms per op name, groups are non-empty so no empty aggregates.
Nested lambda `x => x.Ms` in gr.Sum: finite doubles.
Lambda `x => x.Total` OrderByDescending then Take(5): ranks by total time, not count, as the header states.

Lambda `x => Invariant($"{Escape(x.Name)}x{x.Count} ({x.Total:F1}ms)")`: invariant formatting inside FormattableString.Invariant, name escaped; the multiplication sign is non-ASCII but the file is UTF-8 (File.WriteAllText default).
Lambda `d => d.Ms` Sum for the total: empty list gives 0, no exception.
Lambda `f => f.Gen` OrderBy for the folder table: numeric order of generations.

Function: PerfAnalyzeReport.public static void WriteJson(string path, PerfAnalyze.AnalysisResult result)
Rationale: WriteJson: serialises an anonymous projection with the NaN-as-null converter (so empty groups do not throw) via invariant System.Text.Json. Schema inconsistency: top-level and group members are camelCase (csvFileCount, firstVisualMs, kindCounts) but the folder rows (Gen, T1CatalogReadyMs, T2Ms, T3Phase, T3Ms) and startup rows (Phase, Median, Min, Max, Count) are PascalCase because the anonymous types use member-name inference, so a consumer keyed on camelCase silently misses them. File written non-atomically with File.WriteAllText after summary.md. See PA-05. Covered by PerfAnalyzeReportTests.DroppedRowsAreSurfacedInMarkdownAndJson and PerfAnalyzeTests.PerfAnalyzeOnTheSampleDirectoryWritesSummaryMdAndJson (no schema-casing assertion).
Lambda `g => new { scenario, mode, cond, ... }`: projects every group field; slowestDecilePhaseShare and kindCounts are dictionaries with double/int values passing through the NaN converter.
Lambda `f => new { f.Gen, f.T1CatalogReadyMs, f.T2Ms, f.T3Phase, f.T3Ms }`: member-name inference emits PascalCase JSON keys (Gen, T1CatalogReadyMs...) unlike the camelCase siblings; part of PA-05.
Lambda `p => new { p.Phase, p.Median, p.Min, p.Max, p.Count }` over StartupPhases tuples: PascalCase keys (Phase, Median, Min, Max, Count) unlike camelCase siblings; part of PA-05.

Lambda `r => new { r.Rule, r.Triggered, r.Evidence, r.Note }`: PascalCase keys (Rule, Triggered, Evidence, Note) next to camelCase group members; Triggered is bool? so N/A serialises as null (correct); part of PA-05.

Function: PerfAnalyzeReport.internal static IEnumerable<(string Phase, double Median, double Min, double Max, int Count)> StartupPhases(GroupSummary summary)
Rationale: StartupPhases: groups all runs' Startup dictionaries by phase, sorts values, median with correct even/odd handling (sorted[mid-1]+sorted[mid])/2; groups are non-empty so sorted[0]/[^1] are safe; results ordered by median. Covered by PerfAnalyzeTests.BuildsStartupMilestonesAndMapsFirstPresentedOntoTheProcessStartTimeline (builder side); report side by sample-directory test.
Lambda `run => run` SelectMany flattening the per-run phase dictionaries into key/value pairs.
Lambda `kv => kv.Key` GroupBy key with Ordinal comparer.
Lambda `kv => kv.Value` GroupBy element selector: ms since process start.
Lambda `group => {...}` Select computing median/min/max/count tuple; median arithmetic uses doubles so no integer overflow or truncation.
Lambda `v => v` OrderBy ascending for the median.
Lambda `p => p.Item2` OrderBy median (the tuple's second element, named Median in the declared return type); deterministic for ties by group order.

Function: PerfAnalyzeReport.private static double PercentileOrNaN(List<double> sortedAsc, double p)
Rationale: PercentileOrNaN: NaN for empty sorted list instead of calling NearestRank with an empty list; otherwise NearestRank percentile on pre-sorted data.
Ms: null or NaN renders N/A, otherwise F1 with InvariantCulture; +/-Infinity cannot occur (inputs filtered finite) and would print as 'Infinity' only for a bug elsewhere.
Pct: NaN renders N/A, else value*100 with F1 InvariantCulture and a % suffix; HitRate is in [0,1].

Escape: replaces '|' with '\|' and CR/LF with spaces so a scenario/alias/evidence string cannot break the Markdown table; does not escape backticks or backslashes (cosmetic). Covered by PerfAnalyzeReportTests.PipeInAGroupNameIsEscapedSoTheTableKeepsItsColumns.
RulesConfig private ctor: stores the already-built nested dictionary; only Load/Default construct it, so _data is never null.

Function: RulesConfig.public double Get(string rule, string key, double @default)
Rationale: Get: returns the configured number when both rule and key exist, otherwise the caller's default; rule and key lookups are case-sensitive (JSON keys must match exactly, a typo silently falls back to the default); no range validation, so a negative or zero threshold from the rules file is accepted. Covered by PerfAnalyzeTests.RulesConfigOverridesDefaultThresholds.

Load: File.ReadAllText then Deserialize into a nullable-section map; JsonException (bad JSON, wrong value types) is wrapped in InvalidDataException naming the file, null sections mean defaults, a top-level JSON null yields an empty config; a missing file surfaces as FileNotFoundException and a directory path as UnauthorizedAccessException (unwrapped, fine for CLI). Covered by RulesConfigOverridesDefaultThresholds and BenchmarkReportFormattingTests.PerfAnalyzeArguments_BadRulesAreRejected (argument side).
Default: empty config so every Get returns its built-in default; trivial.

FmtMs: null or NaN renders N/A, otherwise F1 invariant with ms suffix, so evidence never prints empty text or NaN. Covered by PerfAnalyzeReportTests.RUiEvidenceShowsNaForAnAbsentRamHitP95 and RFolderEvidenceShowsNaForMissingT1AndT3.

Function: PerfRules.public static RuleResult EvaluateRIo(RulesConfig cfg, IReadOnlyList<NavRecord> sourceMissNavs)
Rationale: EvaluateRIo: eligible navs need FinalVisualMs>0 (no divide by zero) and TReadMs; N/A with an explanatory note when none (t_read only exists under PHOTOREVIEW_DIAG_PREREAD); averages per-nav ratios not a ratio of sums, threshold default 40 percent; invariant formatting. Affected indirectly by PA-01 (t_read share itself is unaffected, the t_decode side is). Covered by PerfAnalyzeTests.RIoTriggersOnHighIoShareAndIsNotTriggeredBelowThreshold and RIoIsNotApplicableWithoutReadTiming.
Lambda `n => n.FinalVisualMs is > 0 && n.TReadMs.HasValue`: excludes zero/negative/absent final times and absent reads, making the following division safe.
Lambda `n => n.TReadMs!.Value / n.FinalVisualMs!.Value`: both values proven non-null and the divisor >0 by the Where.

Function: PerfRules.public static RuleResult EvaluateRDec(RulesConfig cfg, IReadOnlyList<NavRecord> decodeNavs)
Rationale: EvaluateRDec: same eligibility pattern (FinalVisualMs>0 and TDecodeMs present), N/A when none, avg share vs decodeSharePct default 40; the TDecodeMs input is biased low under PHOTOREVIEW_DIAG_PREREAD because of PA-01. Covered by RDecTriggersOnHighDecodeShareAndIsNotTriggeredBelowThreshold.
Lambda `n => n.FinalVisualMs is > 0 && n.TDecodeMs.HasValue`: guards the divisor.
Lambda `n => n.TDecodeMs!.Value / n.FinalVisualMs!.Value`: safe after the filter.

Function: PerfRules.public static RuleResult EvaluateRUi(RulesConfig cfg, IReadOnlyList<NavRecord> ramHitNavs, double ramHitFinalP95, double? frameTimeP95Ms)
Rationale: EvaluateRUi: share of (t_input+t_assign+t_render) in final visual time (missing parts count as 0), RamHit P95 and frame-time P95 each tested against thresholds; returns N/A only when all three inputs are absent, otherwise OR of the three; NaN ramHitFinalP95 is guarded explicitly before comparison; nested Invariant formatting is redundant but correct. Covered by RUiTriggersOnHighUiShareOrHighRamHitP95AndIsNotTriggeredOtherwise and RUiTriggersOnHighFrameTimeAlone.
Lambda `n => n.FinalVisualMs is > 0`: non-positive finals excluded to protect the division.

Lambda `n => ((TInputMs ?? 0)+(TAssignMs ?? 0)+(TRenderMs ?? 0)) / n.FinalVisualMs!.Value`: divisor >0 by the Where; TInputMs measured from the key press is part of FinalVisualMs because t0 is the matched KeyInput, so the share is internally consistent.

Function: PerfRules.public static RuleResult EvaluateRPre(RulesConfig cfg, double ramHitFinalP95, double nonRamHitSharePct, bool isBurstScenario)
Rationale: EvaluateRPre: N/A when there is no RamHit P95; otherwise triggered if RamHit P95 <= ramHitP95MaxMs and the non-RamHit share >= threshold (S3/S4 default 30, S2 default 10 percent); NaN nonRamHitSharePct yields false (comparison with NaN), which cannot happen once a RamHit P95 exists. Covered by RPreTriggersOnFastRamHitWithLowCoverageAndIsNotTriggeredWithGoodCoverage.

Function: PerfRules.public static RuleResult EvaluateRCont(RulesConfig cfg, double? decodeMsLowWorkers, double? decodeMsHighWorkers, int? lowWorkers, int? highWorkers)
Rationale: EvaluateRCont: N/A when either decode average is missing or the two worker counts are equal (including both null); ratio=high/max(low,0.0001) so a zero-ms low-worker average cannot divide by zero (it yields a huge ratio, which is arguably correct); default factor 1.3; invariant formatting of nullable doubles with F1 works. Covered by RContTriggersOnDecodeSlowdownAndIsNotTriggeredWhenStable and RContIsNotApplicableWithoutTwoDistinctWorkerRuns.

Function: PerfRules.public static RuleResult EvaluateRThread(RulesConfig cfg, int dispatcherLongOpCount, double? tInputP95Ms)
Rationale: EvaluateRThread: triggers when dispatcherLongOpCount>0 OR t_input P95>inputP95Ms (default 16), N/A only if there is no long op and no t_input. The XML doc says 'repeated DispatcherLongOp during S2/S3', but a single long op in any scenario (the caller already applied the ms threshold) flags the group, and there is no configurable count threshold, so one stray 17 ms dispatcher op marks R-THREAD true. Possibly intentional (D11 spec not available in the repo anymore) so not proven wrong. See PA-03. Covered by RThreadTriggersOnDispatcherLongOpsOrHighInputP95AndIsNotTriggeredOtherwise (asserts counts 3 and 0 only; a single long op is untested).

Function: PerfRules.public static RuleResult EvaluateRGc(RulesConfig cfg, double? gcTimePercent)
Rationale: EvaluateRGc: null gcTimePercent gives N/A, else >= gcTimePct (default 10); the value comes from process.json unvalidated (negative or above 100 accepted) which only affects a diagnostic flag. Covered by RGcTriggersAboveThresholdAndIsNotTriggeredBelow.

Function: PerfRules.public static RuleResult EvaluateRDisk(RulesConfig cfg, IReadOnlyList<NavRecord> diskCacheHitNavs, IReadOnlyList<NavRecord> sourceMissNavs)
Rationale: EvaluateRDisk: compares avg t_disk of DiskCacheHit navs with avg (t_read ?? 0)+t_decode of SourceMiss navs times a factor (default 1.0); N/A unless both sets are non-empty so Average never runs on empty; the read+decode sum is biased low under PA-01 because decode already had the read removed. Covered by RDiskTriggersWhenDiskCacheIsNoFasterThanReDecodingAndIsNotTriggeredOtherwise.
Lambda `n => n.TDiskMs.HasValue` keeps DiskCacheHit navs that actually carry a disk time.
Lambda `n => n.TDiskMs!.Value` safe after the HasValue filter.
Lambda `n => n.TDecodeMs.HasValue` keeps SourceMiss navs with a decode time.
Lambda `n => (n.TReadMs ?? 0) + n.TDecodeMs!.Value`: missing read counts as 0, decode non-null by the Where.

Function: PerfRules.public static RuleResult EvaluateRFolder(RulesConfig cfg, IReadOnlyList<FolderGenSummary> gens)
Rationale: EvaluateRFolder: N/A when no generation has T2; worst T2 via MaxBy compared strictly greater than folderT0ToT2Ms (default 1000 ms); evidence uses FmtMs so missing T1/T3 print N/A. Covered by RFolderTriggersOnSlowFolderOpenAndIsNotTriggeredWhenFast and RFolderEvidenceShowsNaForMissingT1AndT3.
Lambda `g => g.T2Ms.HasValue` selects generations with a measured first present.
Lambda `g => g.T2Ms` for MaxBy over double?; the preceding filter guarantees values, `worst` cannot be null on a non-empty list.

RunFileMeta.Load: reads sibling session.json/process.json read-only, tolerates malformed/partial/unreadable files (catch limited to Json/IO/Unauthorized/InvalidOperation), recovers condition from the run-matrix directory name, workers from session.json or the CSV header diag flags, folderAlias keeps fixtures from being pooled, gc percent computed only when elapsedMs>0. Values are not range-checked (negative workers, gc percent above 100, NaN-free but absurd numbers accepted) which only affects diagnostics grouping. Covered by PerfAnalyzeTests.PerfAnalyzeKeepsWorkerTreatmentsSeparateAndOnlyComparesSameCondition and the sample-directory test.

Function: RunFileMeta.private static string? GetString(JsonElement e, string name)
Rationale: GetString: returns the string value only for JsonValueKind.String properties, null otherwise, so a number-typed scenario falls back to the next key or default; no exceptions.

Function: PerfStats.public static double NearestRank(IReadOnlyList<double> sortedAscending, double percentile)
Rationale: NearestRank: empty list or NaN percentile gives NaN, percentile clamped to [0,100], rank = ceil(p*n/100) multiplied-first so 7 percent of 100 is exactly rank 7, rank clamped to [1,n] before indexing; input must already be sorted (callers sort). Covered extensively by BenchmarkStatisticsEdgeTests.NearestRank_* and PerfAnalyzeTests.NearestRankPercentileMatchesHandComputedExpectations / NearestRankOfEmptySequenceIsNaN.

SlowestDecilePhaseShare: eligible navs need FinalVisualMs>0, slice = max(1, ceil(count*0.10)) of the slowest (checked ceil(n*0.1) equals n/10 for every multiple of 10 up to 2000, so no float overshoot), per-phase mean share over the slice treating absent phases as 0 but omitting phases absent for the whole slice. Covered by PerfAnalyzeTests.SlowestDecilePhaseShareMatchesHandComputedRatiosForOneNav and SlowestDecilePhaseShareOnlyAveragesTheSlowestTenPercent.
Lambda `n => n.FinalVisualMs is > 0`: protects the share division.
Lambda `n => n.FinalVisualMs` OrderBy over double?: nulls are filtered earlier so ordering is by value; stable for ties.
Lambda `n => get(n).HasValue` Any: skips a phase measured by no nav in the slice.
Lambda `n => (get(n) ?? 0.0) / n.FinalVisualMs!.Value`: divisor >0 by the eligibility filter; share may exceed 1 for overlapping phases (documented as mean t_x/finalVisual).

GroupKey.ToString: Scenario/Mode/Cond/workers=N with the worker count formatted invariantly and '?' when unknown, so group labels in Markdown are locale-independent.

LowSampleWarning: `Count < 20` where Count includes Incomplete navs, but every percentile in the group is computed from complete navs only; a group with 25 navs of which 15 are incomplete shows no N<20 warning although P95 is the max of 10 samples. See PA-02. Covered by sample-directory tests only for the happy path; no test for incomplete-heavy groups.

Function: GroupSummary.public static GroupSummary Build(GroupKey key, List<NavRecord> navs)
Rationale: GroupSummary.Build: percentiles/max only when the sorted list is non-empty (NaN otherwise, serialised as null), KindCounts and HitRate over complete navs, HitRate guarded by complete.Count>0 so no division by zero, SlowestDecilePhaseShare delegated; 'RamHit' substring counts Thumbnail+RamHit as a hit. Covered by PerfAnalyzeTests.IncompleteNavsAreExcludedFromPercentilesButStillCounted.

Lambda `n => !n.Incomplete`: complete set used by every percentile.
Lambda `n => n.FirstVisualMs is not null` (firsts Where): complete navs always have it, guard avoids null.
Lambda `n => n.FirstVisualMs!.Value`: safe after the filter.

Lambda `n => n.FinalVisualMs is not null` (finals Where).
Lambda `n => n.FinalVisualMs!.Value`: safe after the filter.
Lambda `v => v` ascending sort of finals.
Lambda `n => n.TRenderFrameMs is not null`: older CSVs lack RenderedFrame so the group's renderedFrame stats stay NaN (N/A) instead of 0.
Lambda `n => n.TRenderFrameMs!.Value`: safe after the filter.

Lambda `n => n.Kind` Select for the KindCounts tally; Kind defaults to "Unknown" so the key is never null.

Function: SlowLinkFileSystem.public bool TryCopyNew(string source, string destination, CopyCreationProof proof)
